title: Curiosity's Selfie at Mont Mercou
description_short: NASA's Curiosity rover takes a selfie on Mars in front of Mont Mercou, a rock outcrop about 6 meters tall.
notes: Well-known color selfie (March 2021) with a dramatic cliff behind the rover. Credit taken from the record's secondary_creator field.

title: Sunset in Mars Gale Crater
description_short: The Sun sets inside a cool blue glow above the dark horizon of Gale Crater on Mars, seen by the Curiosity rover.
notes: Curiosity's first color sunset, the classic blue Mars sunset (taken 15 Apr 2015, sol 956; record date is the release date). Credit names university partner Texas A&M alongside NASA. No ~medium rendition exists for this asset (403), so url_medium points to ~orig.jpg (1344x1080 px, 52 KB).

title: Shades of Martian Darkness
description_short: Six simulated views show the Martian sky getting darker and the Sun fading to a tiny dot during the 2018 global dust storm.
notes: The ID named in the brief. It is a simulation of Opportunity's view (opacity tau 1 to 11), not a camera photo - say so on the card. Credit names TAMU (Texas A&M) alongside NASA. No ~medium rendition exists (403), so url_medium points to ~orig.jpg (1500x1000 px, 215 KB). Real-photo alternative that has ~medium: PIA22520, Curiosity before/after views, NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS.

title: InSight's Final Selfie
description_short: NASA's InSight lander on Mars takes its final selfie, with its solar panels covered in a thick layer of dust.
notes: InSight's last selfie (taken 24 Apr 2022, sol 1211); shows the dust build-up that cut its power. Credit taken from secondary_creator.

title: MOXIE All Tucked In
description_short: The shiny gold-plated MOXIE instrument, which makes oxygen from Martian air, sits installed inside NASA's Perseverance rover.
notes: Clearest close-up of the real flight instrument (gold box with intake tubes). Credit taken from secondary_creator. Alternative showing engineers lowering it into the rover: PIA24176 (no ~medium rendition).

title: Major Solar Flare
description_short: A giant X9.3 solar flare flashes brightly on the Sun on 6 September 2017, seen by NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory.
notes: CAVEAT: the library holds no SDO flare image from May 2024 or 3 Oct 2024 (searched flare / SDO / X-class / Solar Dynamics Observatory with 2018-2026 date filters). This is the X9.3 flare of 6 Sep 2017 (the record calls it the largest solar flare of the last decade), so the card text must say 2017. Center field is JPL (Photojournal host) but the credit is GSFC/SDO. Bright straight lines in the picture are instrument artifacts from the flash.

title: iss055e000821
description_short: NASA astronaut Scott Tingle checks red lettuce growing in the Veggie plant chamber on the International Space Station.
notes: Astronaut together with growing lettuce in Veggie (Veg-03, 3 Mar 2018). Record has no explicit credit line (center JSC), so the library default 'NASA' is used. No photographer field; the record title is just the ID.

title: iss064e016025
description_short: A radish bulb is visible among leafy radish plants growing inside the Advanced Plant Habitat on the International Space Station.
notes: Plant Habitat-02 radishes with a bulb in view (27 Dec 2020); in NASA's Plants_In_Space album. Record has no explicit credit line (center JSC), so the library default 'NASA' is used. No photographer field; the record title is just the ID. Alternative with astronaut Kate Rubins beside the habitat: iss064e004997.

title: Zinnia flower in Columbus module
description_short: A zinnia flower grown in the Veggie garden blooms aboard the International Space Station, photographed in close-up by astronaut Scott Kelly.
notes: Close-up taken 22 Jan 2016 with flash, so colors should be natural; in NASA's Plants_In_Space album. Record has no credit line; its photographer field is 'Scott Kelly' (NASA astronaut), center JSC, so 'NASA' is used ('NASA/Scott Kelly' would also fit).

title: Artemis I Flight Day 13: Orion, Earth, and Moon
description_short: Part of the Artemis I Orion spacecraft is seen with the Moon and Earth in the distance, at its farthest point from Earth.
notes: Iconic Artemis I flight-day-13 view (28 Nov 2022) from a solar-array camera, 268,563 miles from Earth. Record has no explicit credit line (center JSC), so the library default 'NASA' is used. An Artemis II equivalent also exists in the library: art002e009567, 'Orion POV: Destination and Home', 6 Apr 2026, whose description says 'Credit: NASA' (small and medium renditions available).

title: The Lunar South Pole
description_short: A mosaic from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter shows the heavily cratered region around the Moon's south pole, about 600 kilometers across.
notes: LROC Wide Angle Camera mosaic of the south polar region, about 600 km wide; Shackleton crater lies at the pole. The library description is only the title; details confirmed on the NASA Photojournal page for PIA13523. Credit names Arizona State University (camera operator) alongside NASA/GSFC.

title: Apollo 8 Mission image, Earth over the horizon of the moon
description_short: The blue-and-white Earth rises above the gray horizon of the Moon, photographed by the Apollo 8 crew on 24 December 1968.
notes: The original Apollo 8 'Earthrise' color frame AS08-14-2383. Record has no explicit credit line (center JSC), so the library default 'NASA' is used.

title: Interior view of "mail box" for purging carbon dioxide from Lunar Module
description_short: Inside the Apollo 13 Lunar Module, the makeshift "mailbox" device uses a Command Module canister to clean carbon dioxide from the air.
notes: The real in-flight device photographed by the crew (April 1970), not the ground prototype (S70-35013 shows that one in Mission Control). Record has no explicit credit line (center JSC), so the library default 'NASA' is used.

title: Artemis I MARES Payloads - Install into Crew Module
description_short: Two radiation-test mannequins, Helga and Zohar, sit installed in the passenger seats inside the Artemis I Orion crew capsule.
notes: Both manikins in their Orion seats (8 Aug 2022), 35 mm framing; Zohar is the one wearing the AstroRad vest. Credit taken from the record's photographer / IPTC credit field. The MARE experiment is a DLR / Israel Space Agency partnership, but the photo itself is NASA's.

title: WATSON Documents First Sample on the Martian Surface
description_short: A metal sample tube filled with Martian rock lies on the surface of Mars, where the Perseverance rover placed it.
notes: First sample tube dropped at the Three Forks depot (21 Dec 2022), imaged by the WATSON arm camera. Very wide picture (4784x1666 px, about 2.9:1) - letterbox it rather than crop. 16:9 alternative showing two drill holes in the rock Rochette: PIA24840, NASA/JPL-Caltech.

title: Astronaut Harrison Schmitt retrieving lunar samples during EVA
description_short: Apollo 17 astronaut Harrison Schmitt carries a sampling scoop across the Moon's surface to collect a rock sample in December 1972.
notes: Astronaut actually at work collecting samples (EVA-2, Station 5, 12 Dec 1972), photographed by Gene Cernan. Record has no explicit credit line (center JSC), so the library default 'NASA' is used. Alternative with a huge boulder: as17-146-22294.

title: Curiosity Sees Streaks and Specks During 2024 Solar Storm
description_short: White streaks and specks cover a black-and-white Curiosity navigation-camera view of Mars, made by solar-storm particles hitting the camera on 20 May 2024.
notes: Frame of a three-frame navcam video taken on 20 May 2024 (sol 4,190); the record says RAD measured its biggest radiation surge since landing at this time, matching the card. Credit from secondary_creator. No ~medium rendition (403), so url_medium points to ~orig.jpg (114 KB).

title: Solar Storm Triggers Whole-Planet Aurora at Mars
description_short: Two views of Mars in ultraviolet light from NASA's MAVEN spacecraft: before and during the bright whole-planet aurora of September 2017.
notes: Real MAVEN IUVS ultraviolet data in a purple-white colour scheme on top of a simulated image of Mars (the record says so), not an ordinary photo. No library image of the 2024 Perseverance green aurora was found. Credit from secondary_creator. No ~medium (403), so url_medium points to ~orig.jpg (272 KB; ~small is 40 KB and is what the script downloads).

title: Tycho Supernova Remnant (Chandra X-ray image)
description_short: A glowing round cloud of hot gas left over from a star that exploded in our galaxy, seen in X-rays by NASA's Chandra observatory.
notes: Record title is generic ('History of Chandra X-Ray Observatory'), so the title is written from the description. Shows the debris of the supernova seen by Tycho Brahe in 1572; supernova remnants like this are where galactic cosmic rays are thought to get their speed. The picture does not show cosmic rays themselves. X-ray colours are false colours (red/green/blue = low/medium/high energy). Record (MSFC) has no credit line, so the library default NASA is used.

title: Astronaut Anne McClain wears an experimental wearable dosimeter
description_short: NASA astronaut Anne McClain wears a small experimental dosimeter that measures her radiation dose in real time on the Space Station.
notes: Taken 1 Apr 2025 in the Destiny module. Record has no explicit credit line (center JSC), so the library default NASA is used.

title: Close-up view of astronauts footprint in lunar soil
description_short: A bootprint pressed into the fine grey soil, called regolith, on the Moon during the Apollo 11 moonwalk.
notes: Classic Apollo 11 bootprint (20 Jul 1969). Shows what regolith looks like; it is not a shelter or a shield. Record has no explicit credit line (center JSC), so the library default NASA is used.

title: Dust Storm Covers Opportunity
description_short: A global map of Mars from orbit shows a dust storm spreading over the planet on 6 June 2018; a blue dot marks the Opportunity rover.
notes: Real MARCI camera map from Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, chosen over the existing img-dust-storm-2018 entry because that one is a simulation. Credit from secondary_creator.

title: Fission Surface Power Technology Demonstration Unit
description_short: A NASA Glenn technician works on a 10-kilowatt Stirling power converter, part of a ground test unit for a fission power system for the Moon or Mars.
notes: Real ground-test hardware (record date 9 Nov 2016), not a reactor on the Moon. The record says a flight system would make 40 kW, matching the card's earlier 40 kW goal. Record (GRC) has no credit line, so the library default NASA is used.

title: Blood Moon lunar eclipse 2025
description_short: Seven photos combined show the Moon turning red as it slides into Earth's shadow during the total lunar eclipse of 14 March 2025, seen from New Orleans.
notes: Same eclipse as the card, but seen from Earth (NASA Michoud Assembly Facility), not from the Blue Ghost lander; the library has no Blue Ghost eclipse image. Composite of 7 exposures, very wide (640x236 small). Credit from photographer field.

title: Victor Glover on the battery-upgrade spacewalk
description_short: NASA astronaut Victor Glover works outside the Space Station on 1 February 2021, during the spacewalk that finished the battery upgrade.
notes: Record title is just the ID; title written from the description. Same date as the card's final battery spacewalk. Record has no explicit credit line (center JSC), so the library default NASA is used.

title: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter cameras before launch
description_short: Before launch in 2009, a technician checks the thermal blanket around the LROC camera on NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter.
notes: Record title is just the ID; title written from the description. Shows the LROC Narrow Angle Camera, the camera the meteoroid hit in October 2014 (the hit itself has no library picture). Record (KSC) has no credit line, so the library default NASA is used.

title: Spacewalkers inspect the Soyuz MS-09
description_short: On 11 December 2018 two cosmonauts on a spacewalk examine the outside of the Soyuz MS-09 spacecraft, where the small hole had been found from inside in August.
notes: Record title is just the ID; title written from the description. Photo is from the later inspection spacewalk, not from the night of the leak; the record says the hole was sealed from inside within hours. Record has no explicit credit line (center JSC), so the library default NASA is used.

title: Astronaut Suni Williams replaces particulate filters on the water recovery system
description_short: NASA astronaut Suni Williams replaces filters on the water recovery system in the Space Station's bathroom area.
notes: Taken 1 Nov 2024 in the Tranquility module. Record has no explicit credit line (center JSC), so the library default NASA is used.

title: Jessica Watkins eats a meal on the Space Station
description_short: NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins eats a meal aboard the International Space Station.
notes: Record title is just the ID; title written from the description. Illustrates food, one of the daily needs on the card. Taken 4 Oct 2022. Record has no explicit credit line (center JSC), so the library default NASA is used.

title: Mars 2020 Liftoff
description_short: An Atlas V rocket launches NASA's Perseverance rover to Mars on 30 July 2020, during that year's Mars launch window.
notes: Credit from photographer field.

title: Earth and Its Moon, as Seen From Mars
description_short: Earth and its Moon seen from Mars by the HiRISE camera on NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter on 20 November 2016.
notes: Composite of the best Earth and Moon frames; the Moon was brightened so it shows (the record says so), sizes and positions are true. Credit from secondary_creator. No ~small or ~medium rendition (403), so both URLs point to ~orig.jpg (657x358 px, 12 KB).

title: Curiosity's Hazcams Capture a Day on Mars
description_short: Curiosity's hazard cameras record 12 hours of one Mars day on 8 November 2023, using commands sent before solar conjunction began.
notes: Frame from a Hazcam video; the record says these were among the last commands sent before the 2023 conjunction pause, matching the card. Credit from secondary_creator. No ~medium (403), so url_medium points to ~orig.jpg (106 KB).

title: Tracks of a Giant
description_short: The giant 70-metre dish at NASA's Deep Space Network site in Goldstone, California, tracks a spacecraft on 17 November 2009.
notes: Deep Space Station 14, nicknamed the Mars antenna. Credit from secondary_creator. No ~medium (403), so url_medium points to ~orig.jpg (177 KB; ~small is 23 KB).

title: InSight Images a Sunrise on Mars
description_short: Sunrise on Mars photographed by NASA's InSight lander on its 145th sol, around 5:30 in the morning Mars time.
notes: Taken 24 Apr 2019 (record date is the release date). Credit from secondary_creator. No ~medium (403), so url_medium points to ~orig.jpg (60 KB).

title: Perseverance's Mast Microphone
description_short: The small microphone on the mast of NASA's Perseverance rover, part of the SuperCam instrument.
notes: Photo of the actual mast microphone. Credit from secondary_creator.

title: InSight's Seismometer on the Martian Surface
description_short: The dome-shaped shield covering NASA InSight's seismometer on the surface of Mars, on the mission's 110th sol.
notes: The seismometer (SEIS) sits under this wind and thermal shield. Credit from secondary_creator. No ~medium (403), so url_medium points to ~orig.jpg (154 KB; ~small is 60 KB).

title: Kuipers exercises on the ARED
description_short: ESA astronaut Andre Kuipers exercises on the advanced Resistive Exercise Device, the Space Station's weight-lifting machine.
notes: Taken 5 Jun 2012 in the Tranquility node. Record has no explicit credit line (center JSC), so the library default NASA is used.

title: Mark and Scott Kelly talk to news media
description_short: Astronaut Scott Kelly and his identical twin brother, former astronaut Mark Kelly, talk to reporters before Scott's one-year mission.
notes: Taken 19 Jan 2015 at Johnson Space Center. Credit from photographer field (Robert Markowitz, NASA JSC).

title: Mars Weather-Station Tools on Rover Mast
description_short: One of the weather-station booms of REMS sticks out to the side from the mast of NASA's Curiosity rover.
notes: Detail from a January 2015 Curiosity self-portrait (PIA19142). Credit from secondary_creator. No ~small or ~medium rendition (403), so both URLs point to ~orig.jpg (1021x562 px, 110 KB).

title: Curiosity Views Sulfur Crystals Within a Crushed Rock
description_short: Yellow crystals of pure sulfur inside a rock that Curiosity cracked open by driving over it, seen on 7 June 2024.
notes: Mastcam view of 'Convict Lake', about 13 cm across; colour adjusted to look as on Earth (the record says so). Credit from secondary_creator.

title: Curiosity Finds Iron Meteorite on Mars
description_short: The iron meteorite 'Lebanon', about 2 metres wide, lying on the ground of Mars, seen by NASA's Curiosity rover.
notes: Mastcam colour view with ChemCam close-up insets, hence the long partner credit (from secondary_creator).

title: Rock Outcrops on Mars and Earth
description_short: The 'Link' rock on Mars, full of rounded pebbles (left), next to a similar pebble rock from a stream on Earth (right).
notes: Side-by-side comparison released 27 Sep 2012; the right half is an Earth photo, which the title makes clear. Credit from secondary_creator.

title: Butte M9a in Murray Buttes on Mars
description_short: A flat-topped sandstone hill called butte M9a in the Murray Buttes on Mars, seen by Curiosity on 1 September 2016.
notes: Mastcam telephoto mosaic. Credit from secondary_creator.

title: Lobate Scarps on the Moon
description_short: Step-shaped cliffs called lobate scarps near Mare Frigoris on the Moon, photographed by NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter.
notes: These are the fault scarps formed as the Moon shrinks. Credit from secondary_creator (NASA). No ~medium (403), so url_medium points to ~orig.jpg (268 KB; ~small is 56 KB).

title: View of the orange soil which Apollo 17 crewmen found at Station 4 during EVA
description_short: The orange soil found by the Apollo 17 crew at Shorty Crater on 12 December 1972, with a geology tool for scale and colour.
notes: The tripod-like gnomon gives scale and true colour. Record has no explicit credit line (center JSC), so the library default NASA is used.

title: Apollo 15 lunar sample 15415, the Genesis Rock
description_short: The white Genesis Rock (Apollo 15 sample 15415) inside a sealed lab cabinet on Earth in August 1971.
notes: Record title is all capitals ('APOLLO XV - LUNAR SAMPLE (NO. 15415 - GENESIS ROCK)'), so it was rewritten. Record has no explicit credit line (center JSC), so the library default NASA is used.

title: Lunar Roving Vehicle photographed against lunar background during EVA
description_short: The Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle parked on the Moon at Hadley-Apennine, with Mount Hadley in the distance.
notes: Taken during the third moonwalk (31 Jul - 2 Aug 1971). Record has no explicit credit line (center JSC), so the library default NASA is used.

title: CHAPEA Mission 2 Crew Exits Habitat After Yearlong Stay
description_short: The four CHAPEA crew members stand outside the 3D-printed Mars Dune Alpha habitat after leaving it on 31 October 2026, after 378 days inside.
notes: Second CHAPEA crew; the record's own credit line is 'NASA/James Blair'.

title: Butch Wilmore with the first 3D printer in space
description_short: Astronaut Butch Wilmore holds a printed test piece next to the new 3D printer on the International Space Station in December 2014.
notes: Record title is '3D Printer Coupon removal and stowage'; title written from the description. Photographer field is Barry Wilmore (NASA astronaut), so the credit follows the img-zinnia precedent: NASA.

title: Artemis I Orion Post-Flight Payload Processing - MARE
description_short: After flying around the Moon on Artemis I, the test manikins Helga and Zohar are inspected at Kennedy Space Center; Zohar wears the AstroRad vest.
notes: Post-flight inspection on 17 Jan 2023; a different photo from img-helga-zohar (pre-flight, used by another card). Credit from photographer field.

title: Chile Peppers on ISS
description_short: Chile pepper plants with growing peppers in the Advanced Plant Habitat on the International Space Station.
notes: Photographed by astronaut Megan McArthur, released 30 Sep 2021. Credit from photographer field.

title: Apollo 16 ultraviolet camera on the Moon
description_short: Astronaut Charlie Duke stands in the shadow of the lunar module behind the gold-coated ultraviolet camera on the Moon in April 1972.
notes: The record title says John Young, but its description says Charles Duke stands behind the camera and Young took the photo, so the title was rewritten. Record has no explicit credit line (center JSC), so the library default NASA is used.

title: Viewing Spark Generated by ChemCam Laser for Mars Rover
description_short: The ChemCam laser makes a tiny bright spark on a target during a test on Earth, before Curiosity launched.
notes: Lab test photo (2010), not on Mars. Credit from secondary_creator.

title: Perseverance's Mastcam-Z Captures a Phobos Solar Eclipse
description_short: The potato-shaped moon Phobos passes in front of the Sun, filmed from Mars by NASA's Perseverance rover on 2 April 2022.
notes: Frame from the Mastcam-Z eclipse video (record date is the release date). Credit from secondary_creator. No ~medium (403), so url_medium points to ~orig.jpg (16 KB).

title: Two spacesuits in the Quest airlock
description_short: Two NASA spacesuits with their life-support backpacks wait in the Space Station's Quest airlock, where spacewalks begin.
notes: Record title is just the ID; title written from the description. Taken 20 May 2023. Record has no explicit credit line (center JSC), so the library default NASA is used.

title: Gene Cernan uses the Apollo Lunar Surface Drill
description_short: Apollo 17 commander Gene Cernan works the battery-powered lunar drill on the Moon on 11 December 1972.
notes: Black-and-white frame from the rover's colour TV camera (the record says so), so it is soft. Record title is 'APOLLO 17 - INFLIGHT (1ST EVA)'; title written from the description. Record has no explicit credit line (center JSC), so the library default NASA is used.

title: Microscope view of Apollo 11 Moon rock 10022
description_short: A thin slice of Apollo 11 Moon rock under a microscope: plagioclase (light blue and white), black ilmenite and colourful pyroxene.
notes: Photomicrograph (1969); magnified, and the bright colours come from the microscope lighting, not the rock's real colours. Plagioclase is the aluminium-rich mineral and ilmenite the iron-titanium one named on the card. Record title is 'PHOTO MICROGRAPH - LUNAR SAMPE 10022' (typo, capitals), so it was rewritten. Record has no explicit credit line (center JSC), so the library default NASA is used.
